purpose: Source implementation of CPU shader-clock observation, owned world-frame transport and presentation-domain archive linkage; not runtime certification
sourceBehavior: The exact world screen-context return clears the previous observation and begins a new one only after the original constructor returns its output pointer

Read-only identity resolves the current primary client, both renderer links, level/session epoch, simulation/real timer identities and matching completed native tick/partial/rate/elapsed values; no frozen lease is required
The output context clock pointer and partial must match the selected renderer and client; private addresses/header bytes remain inside native code
The fmod hook records native input/result and the effective value actually returned after any Arctic control, in the approved total/delta/world caller order
Unrelated math callers are ignored; invalid values or recognized out-of-order calls invalidate the observation
A world-pass snapshot requires unchanged primary identity and the matching camera tick/partial/rate/elapsed and renderer-clock bits
The world screen must be the constructed output or its known renderer-owned copy, with matching meaningful header bytes and clock pointer

When world accumulation ran, its original remainder must equal the current native accumulator bits; when skipped, the stored phase must equal its value before the frame and no world remainder may be synthesized
Identity, accumulator and skip flag are rechecked before publication; samples include observation, world sequence and world scope without native addresses
World-hook timing emits the optional sample under nativeTiming.rendererState.shaderClock, including outside frozen playback
Schema 2 brackets the native total input with public-QPC samples in the initialized game epoch domain; snapshots recheck that domain
WorldFrame parsing creates an immutable checked NativeShaderClock with matching world sequence/session/native timing and renderer-clock bits, owned scalar values and false GPU/video readiness
recordingTimelineLimit: Presentation shader time can advance while simulation tick time is held. An archive mapping must preserve those distinct clocks; no fake strictly increasing simulation timestamp or dropped paused-time update is introduced here.
remaining: Authoritative verification of the marker-derived simulation/presentation/relay association; archive source implementation is described in native-shader-clock-history-source.json
Recorded world/absolute shader phase selection during replay reconstruction/export
Native cosmetics phase insertion and resource/material ownership
GPU upload/render and deterministic replay/video verification
